summary: A proposal by Alex McKenzie for a software consulting service for network users. Users with real problems lacked help, because the Resources Notebook updated slowly and technical liaisons were often busy systems programmers. The note describes a service to fill that gap.

plainLanguage.summary: BBN announced an experimental consulting service for people who needed help using network software and resources. Users could contact Nancy Neigus through the Network Control Center or leave an online message.

subtitle: An experimental software consulting service for network users

tldr.problem: Network users with practical problems lacked timely software assistance from existing information and liaison arrangements.
tldr.mechanism: BBN added software consultant Nancy Neigus to the Network Control Center staff to help users with existing network resources.
tldr.outcome: The experimental service could also help check protocol implementations and route reported host software problems.

today: RFC 421 announces an experimental software consulting service at the Network Control Center. The notice says its scope and continued existence would depend on expressed user needs.

sections.title: A Need for User Assistance
sections.content: As network use grew, BBN saw a need for software assistance for users with problems to solve. The Resources Notebook could take a long time to update, while Technical Liaisons were often systems programmers who worked at unusual hours and might not be well suited to answering basic user questions.
sections.plainLanguage: Users needed help that was more timely and approachable than the available documentation and technical contacts. BBN created a service to address that need.

sections.title: An Experimental Consultant Service
sections.content:
BBN added software consultant Nancy Neigus to the Network Control Center staff. She had experience with software on several systems and had spent months learning about network server systems and subsystems.

The RFC says the service was experimental and that its limits and continuation would depend on user needs. Its primary goal was assistance with existing resources, with possible involvement in protocol checks and conflicts also left open.
sections.plainLanguage: Nancy Neigus was available to help people use existing network resources. The service was experimental, and its future depended on whether users found it useful.

sections.title: How to Contact the Service
sections.content: The RFC says Neigus would normally be available on weekdays from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Eastern Time through the Network Control Center telephone. The NCC operators could take messages at other times. Users could also leave an online message at the NIC addressed to NJN, or TIP users could use the Gripe service.
sections.plainLanguage: Users could call during the consultant's stated weekday hours or leave a message through the NCC or NIC. TIP users could also use the Gripe service.
